lines.trans: Well, hello, Samsonov!
Hello! And who are you?
What do you mean, who? I am Sun Tzu.
Samsonov, you have big problems.
This Danya has stepped onto your territory.
And love, Samsonov, is like war. The lawyer is your enemy.
And how can I defeat him?
You did not read my book carefully!
You must strike where the enemy is weak.
You need to lure him onto your territory. Right where you are strong.
And where am I strong?
Well, where did you serve?
In the airborne troops, of course!
That means you have survival skills. And he does not have them!

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'живание'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'survival' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У него есть навыки выживания в лесу.
examples.trans: He has survival skills in the forest.

examples.text: Значит, у тебя есть навыки выживания. А у него их нет!
examples.trans: That means you have survival skills. And he does not have them!

meanings.note: + infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to fight, to brawl', paired with 'подраться'.

examples.text: Ты должен драться за свою любовь.
examples.trans: You must fight for your love.

examples.text: Беги, Самсонов! Ты должен драться за свою любовь.
examples.trans: Run, Samsonov! You must fight for your love.

examples.text: Ваня, тебе нельзя драться на улице!
examples.trans: Vanya, you must not fight on the street!

meanings.note: not to be confused with есть 'there is' (from быть)

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.

зайти.gloss: to come in, to drop in

meanings.en: to come in, to step in

examples.trans: I'll drop by in the evening.

examples.text: Ну, как хочешь. Лидия Алексеевна, зайдите, пожалуйста!
examples.trans: Well, as you like. Lidia Alekseyevna, come in, please!

meanings.en: to lure, to entice into a trap
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'манить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to lure, to entice', paired with 'заманивать'.

examples.text: Надо заманить его на свою территорию.
examples.trans: You need to lure him onto your territory.

examples.text: Надо заманить его на свою территорию. Там, где ты сильный.
examples.trans: You need to lure him onto your territory. Right where you are strong.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'снуть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to fall asleep', paired with 'засыпать'.

examples.text: Опять ты в туалете с книгой заснул!
